title: A 70dB SNDR 80MHz BW Filter-Embedded Pipeline-SAR ADC Achieving 172dB FoMs with Progressive Conversion and Floating-Charge-Transfer Amplifier
problem: Nyquist-sampling ADCs require sharp anti-aliasing filters before digitization, occupying large area and contributing significant noise; continuous-time ΔΣ modulators relax filtering but hit a bandwidth wall due to closed-loop power scaling. Filter-embedded SAR ADCs offer efficiency but are limited to ~tens of MHz sampling, inadequate for wide-bandwidth wireless (>80 MHz).
motivation: Next-generation wireless receivers need high-bandwidth, high-efficiency analog front-ends without bulky baseband filters; high sampling rates enable fewer external components.
method: Filter-embedded pipeline-SAR ADC integrates passive FIR/IIR filtering into the CDAC, providing intrinsic anti-aliasing. Progressive conversion scheme mitigates speed penalties from filtering operations by overlapping multiple stages. Dynamic floating-charge-transfer (FCT) amplifier achieves high-speed residue amplification with high efficiency (no class-AB buffering). Fabricated in 28nm CMOS.
key_novelty: Progressive conversion + floating-charge-transfer amplifier enables filter-embedded operation at 80 MHz bandwidth (4–5x prior bandwidth-limited filter-SAR designs).
contributions: Filter-embedded pipeline-SAR ADC achieves 70.1 dB SNDR over 80 MHz bandwidth
4.9 mW power consumption; 172.2 dB Schreier FoM (high efficiency)
Progressive conversion overlaps filtering and SAR stages to boost sampling rate
Floating-charge-transfer amplifier enables robust high-speed residue amplification

metrics.other: SNDR 70 dB, Schreier FoM 172 dB, OOB suppression >30 dB

baselines: Filter-embedded SAR ADCs (tens of MHz limited)
Nyquist-sampling ADCs with external anti-aliasing filters
limitations: Integration error, mismatch tolerance, and aging robustness not explicitly addressed.
